question.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}\sqrt{z}\,\text{d}S
$$

where $S$ is defined by $z=y-3x$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $3x\le y\le 3.$
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=g(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f(x,y,z)$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

For the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂x}=\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-3x)=-3,
$$

and

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂y}=\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-3x)=1.
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be evaluated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\sqrt{z}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\sqrt{y-3x}\sqrt{1+(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\sqrt{y-3x}\sqrt{11}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{11}{∬}_{D}\,\sqrt{y-3x}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{11}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{3x}^{3}\sqrt{y-3x}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{11}{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{2}{3}(y-3x)^{3/2}]}_{y=3x}^{y=3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{11}}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(3-3x)^{3/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{11}}{3}\,{[\frac{2}{5}\cdot (-\frac{1}{3})(3-3x)^{5/2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{4\sqrt{11}}{45}(0-{3}^{5/2}) \\  & =\frac{4\sqrt{11}}{45}(9\sqrt{3}) \\  & =\frac{4\sqrt{33}}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
